([[Preston, Lancashire]]) | college = * [[Drexel Dragons men's basketball|Drexel]] (2020–2024) * [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 46 | draft_team = [[Orlando Magic]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team2 = →[[Maine Celtics]] | highlights = *3× [[Coastal Athletic Association|CAA]] Defensive Player of the Year (2022–2024) *2× First-team All-CAA (2023, 2024) *Third-team All-CAA (2022) *3× CAA All-Defensive Team (2022–2024) }} '''Amari Williams''' (born 28 January 2002) is a British professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Drexel Dragons men's basketball|Drexel Dragons]] and the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. Williams was selected by the [[Orlando Magic]] with the 46th overall pick in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]], but was immediately traded to the Celtics. ==Early life== Williams grew up in [[Nottingham]], England and initially attended [[Trinity School, Nottingham]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/nottingham-news/meet-six-foot-eight-16-1869443|title=Meet the six foot eight 16-year-old who's a rising star in the basketball world|first=Rod|last=Malcolm|work=[[Nottingham Post]]|date=7 August 2018|access-date=25 October 2024}} and played for his local team the [[Mansfield Giants]]. He transferred to [[Myerscough College]] when he was 16 years old.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/drexel/drexel-basketball-mate-okros-amari-williams-20220114.html|title=Drexel basketball duo's bond stretches from across the pond|first=Ariel|last=Simpson|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=14 January 2022|access-date=25 October 2024}} Williams primarily played [[Association football|football]] when growing up.{{cite web|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/mark-story/article294021474.html|title=Why a 7-foot Englishman could be the key to Mark Pope’s first Kentucky men’s basketball season|first=Mark|last=Story|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|date=17 October 2024|access-date=25 October 2024}} ==College career== ===Drexel=== Williams began his college career with the Drexel Dragons. He was named the [[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) Defensive Player of the Year and third-team all-conference as a sophomore. Williams repeated as CAA Defensive Player of the Year and was named first-team all-conference while averaging 13.7 points, 8.8 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2024/04/21/amari-williams-stats-247-transfer-kentucky-basketball-drexel-dragons-mark-pope-nba-draft/73407020007/|title=Who is Amari Williams? Mark Pope, Kentucky basketball land Drexel star F, per reports|first=John|last=Leuzzi|work=[[Courier Journal]]|date=21 April 2024|access-date=25 October 2024}} As a senior, Williams averaged 12.2 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game and was named the CAA Defensive Player of the Year for a third straight season.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/drexel/drexel-basketball-amari-williams-caa-defensive-player-award-20240307.html|title=Drexel's Amari Williams earns third CAA Defensive Player Award|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=7 March 2024|access-date=25 October 2024}} After the end of the season, Williams decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020–2021 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/drexel/drexel-amari-williams-nba-draft-ncaa-transfer-portal-20240312.html|title=Drexel star forward Amari Williams to see what the NBA draft and NCAA transfer portal might offer|first=Kerith|last=Gabriel|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=12 March 2024|access-date=25 October 2024}} ===Kentucky=== Williams transferred to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39990904/drexel-transfer-amari-williams-commits-kentucky|title=Agent: Drexel transfer Amari Williams commits to Kentucky|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=21 April 2024|access-date=25 October 2024}} He averaged 10.9 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.2 blocks per game while starting in all 36 games he appeared in.{{cite news |last1=Geagan |first1=Matt |title=Celtics draft Amari Williams in second round of NBA Draft |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/amari-williams-boston-celtics-nba-draft/ |access-date=5 July 2025 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=26 June 2025}} In 2025, his Wildcats finished with a 24-12 record. Williams' collegiate career ended with Kentucky's 78-65 loss to Tennessee in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]] Sweet 16. https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/amari-williams-2/gamelog/2025 ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics=== Williams was selected in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]] with the 46th pick by the [[Orlando Magic]] and traded to the [[Boston Celtics]]. He participated in the [[2025 NBA Summer League]] for the Celtics.https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/boston/news/celtics-summer-league-roster-hugo-gonzalez-amari-williams-nba/ On August 15, 2025, [[Boston Celtics]] announced that they had signed Williams to [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Amari Williams to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/081525-celtics-sign-amari-williams-to-two-way-contract|date=August 15, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 15, 2025}} On February 5, 2026, Boston signed Williams to a two-year, $2.7 million standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Celtics' Amari Williams: Inks standard pact with Boston|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-amari-williams-inks-standard-pact-with-boston/|access-date=March 4, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He made 22 appearances (including two starts) for Boston during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 1.4 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 0.5 assists. On June 29, 2026, it was reported that Williams' standard contract team option was being declined by Boston. https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/amari-williams-team-option-getting-declined/ On July 2, the Celtics signed Williams to a new two-way contract. https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20260702-celtics-sign-amari-williams-to-two-way-contract Williams participated in the [[2026 NBA Summer League]] as a member of the Celtics.
